tasks.title: Line graph: sales of books by format
tasks.prompt:
The graph below shows the number of printed books, e-books and audiobooks sold in one country between 2010 and 2022.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

visual.title: Book sales by format, 2010–2022
visual.note: Fictional data created for practice purposes.

examinerNotes: Overview should note: printed books sold far more than the other formats throughout, despite a gradual fall; e-books grew quickly until 2016 and then levelled off; audiobooks grew slowly and then rapidly, almost catching up with e-books.
Audiobooks: 2m → 6m (2016) → 21m (2022), more than ten times higher.
tasks.modelAnswer:
The line graph compares sales of printed books, e-books and audiobooks in one country over a twelve-year period from 2010 to 2022.

Overall, printed books were by far the best-selling format throughout the period, even though their sales gradually declined. E-book sales grew rapidly at first and then remained stable, while audiobooks, which began from a very low level, showed the most impressive growth in the later years.

In 2010, 82 million printed books were sold, compared with just 6 million e-books and 2 million audiobooks. Sales of printed books then fell to 74 million in 2013 and 70 million in 2016, after which they stayed fairly steady, ending at 68 million in 2022.

E-books became popular very quickly: sales almost quadrupled to 22 million by 2013 and reached a peak of 25 million in 2016. After that, however, they levelled off at around 23 to 24 million. Audiobook sales, in contrast, rose only slightly at first, to 6 million in 2016, but then doubled to 12 million in 2019 and reached 21 million in 2022, more than ten times the 2010 figure. By the end of the period, audiobooks were almost as popular as e-books.

tasks.title: Advantages/disadvantages essay: starting your own business
tasks.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

These days, many young people choose to start their own business rather than work for a company.

Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
tasks.modelAnswer:
Thanks to the internet and the success of well-known young entrepreneurs, more and more young people are choosing to set up their own businesses instead of looking for jobs in established companies. Although this path involves real risks, I believe that its advantages generally outweigh its disadvantages.

The most attractive aspect of running one's own business is independence. Young entrepreneurs can work on ideas they are passionate about, make their own decisions and organise their time as they wish, rather than following instructions from a manager. Starting a business also teaches a wide range of skills, from marketing and finance to negotiation and leadership, much faster than an ordinary job would. If the business succeeds, the financial rewards can be far greater than a salary. Furthermore, new businesses benefit society as a whole by creating jobs and introducing new products and services.

On the other hand, there are significant disadvantages. Most new businesses fail within a few years, and young people may lose their savings or borrow money that they struggle to repay. Running a business usually involves long hours and constant stress, especially in the early stages, and there is no fixed income, paid holiday or pension. In addition, young people who start businesses straight after school or university miss the chance to learn from experienced colleagues in a large company.

In my view, these risks are real but worth taking for most young people, because they have fewer responsibilities, such as children or mortgages, than older people and can recover from failure more easily. Even when a business fails, the experience and skills gained are highly valued by employers.

In conclusion, although starting a business is risky and demanding, I believe its benefits, including independence, rapid learning and potential rewards, outweigh the disadvantages for young people.
